outlook.statement: The Company is committed to embedding a futuristic approach that integrates innovation, automation, and artificial intelligence into its operations to enhance productivity, optimize resource efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and create adaptive systems.

The demerger of the Distillery Division into KM Spirits and Allied Industries Limited aims to unlock shareholder value by creating focused entities for sugar and distillery businesses, enabling better operational efficiency, independent growth strategies, and access to capital markets.

Sugarcane development initiatives expected to result in improved sugarcane yield and recovery, enhanced soil health and sustainability, reduction in cultivation cost through mechanization, increased adoption of scientific farming practices, better crop monitoring and timely advisory support to growers, and long-term improvement in cane quality and productivity.

Global sugar market projected to grow at ~1% CAGR (2024-2032), reaching 197.19 million tonnes by 2032. India projected to remain among fastest growing major economies with 6.4% real GDP growth in 2026. Industry seeks MSP revision, stable ethanol policy, liquidity support, export facilitation, and sustainability incentives.

The Board of Directors approved the Scheme of Arrangement for the demerger of the Company's Distillery Division into its wholly owned subsidiary, KM Spirits and Allied Industries Limited, on a going concern basis. The Scheme received no-objection/observations from the Stock Exchanges. The Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad Bench, approved the first motion application and directed convening of meetings of equity shareholders and unsecured creditors. The meeting of equity shareholders was held on May 30, 2026, wherein the Scheme was approved with requisite majority. The Scheme is subject to further necessary approvals, including final sanction of the Hon'ble NCLT and other regulatory authorities.

The Company expects increase in productivity and profits in due course. However, in view of the fact that Sugar Industry is a Govt. controlled industry, giving expected increase in measurable terms is not possible.
